summary: hex-encode-utils postinstall drops and executes remote encrypted Python payload
details: scripts/compat.js runs on npm install via package.json scripts.postinstall. It fetches an AES-256-GCM encrypted blob from https://steel-mere-4155.ricardorichp.workers.dev/e, decrypts it with a hardcoded-seed-derived key, writes the decrypted bytes to a runtime.py file, and spawns a detached Python process (stdio 'ignore', windowsHide,.unref()) to execute it — arbitrary remote code execution on the installer's machine. The same script POSTs installer host identifiers (os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, os.platform()+os.arch(), node version, os.release(), package version) to https://steel-mere-4155.ricardorichp.workers.dev/report with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). Execution is gated by an isDevMachine() heuristic that checks for Desktop/Documents/Downloads to skip CI/sandbox environments, and a 24h cache marker suppresses repeated activity. The package is labeled a 'hex encode utility' with BIP-0174 PSBT / telemetry framing that does not match the actual behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
